title: Radio Reconnaissance Marine (MGySgt to Pvt) NMOS (2621, 2629, 2631, 2641, 2651, 2659, 2691), DIR INTEL
raw_text:
4. MOS 2623, Radio Reconnaissance Marine (MGySgt to Pvt) NMOS (2621, 2629,
2631, 2641, 2651, 2659, 2691), DIR INTEL

    a. Summary. This is an NMOS that requires additional formal training in
reconnaissance, SIGINT (collection, identification, analysis, and reporting),
EW and support to CO while either conducting or in direct support to
reconnaissance operations. Radio Reconnaissance Marines must be able to
extend and enable the national enterprise, conduct full spectrum surveys of
the signal’s environment, provide front end analysis, and facilitate specific
SIGINT/EW/CO missions. Specific skills include planning, coordinating and
executing tactical SIGINT/EW/CO operations. Radio Reconnaissance Marines
will prepare and issue reports to include, translation summaries,
intelligence reports, and technical EW and CO reports as needed. In
addition, Radio Reconnaissance Marines possess proficiency in scout swimming,
small boat operations, patrolling, and long-range communication skills.
Radio Reconnaissance Marines are trained in specialized insertion and
extraction such as high-altitude parachute and combatant dive operations.

       b.   Prerequisites

            (1) No hearing defects.




                                           3-157                     Enclosure (1)
 3122                                                               NAVMC 1200.1L



            (2) Must be a volunteer.

            (3) Must be a U.S. citizen.

            (4) Must currently hold PMOS 2621, 2629, 2631, 2641, 2651, 2659, or
2691.

        (5) Must successfully complete a counter-intelligence scope polygraph
examination.

        (6) Must possess a WSA water survival qualification to enter the
Basic Reconnaissance Course (BRC) (M10AHK2).

        (7) Must possess a WSI water survival qualification to enter the
Reconnaissance Training Assessment Program (RTAP) (M100Z22).

        (8) Security requirement: must have a current single scope
background investigation/T5 investigation and adjudicated for sensitive
compartmented information (SCI) eligibility.

        (9) Must obtain a score of 225 or higher on the physical fitness test
(PFT) to enter RTAP (M100Z22). During RTAP the Marine will be required to
attain a score of 235 or higher on the PFT.

        (10) Must obtain a score of 235 on the physical fitness test (PFT) to
enter BRC and a score of 260 on the combat fitness test (CFT) (accomplished
as part of RTAP). During BRC the student will be required to attain a score
of 250 on the physical fitness test and a score of 270 on the combat fitness
test.

        (11) Must be medically qualified to perform high altitude parachuting
and combatant dive qualifications in accordance with inter-service
requirements established in reference (ai), NAVMED P-117; and reference (at),
Standards of Medical Fitness. The completed NSW/SO physical must be reviewed
and countersigned by an undersea medical officer.

       c.   Requirements

        (1) Complete the Reconnaissance Training Assessment Program
(M100Z22), Camp Pendleton, CA.

        (2) Complete the Basic Reconnaissance Course (BRC) (M10AHK2), Camp
Pendleton, CA.

    d. Duties. For a complete listing of duties and tasks, refer to
reference (r), Signals Intelligence Training and Readiness Manual.

       e.   Related Standard Occupational Classification (SOC) Title and Code

            (1) Command and Control Center Specialists 55-3015.

            (2) Special Forces 55-3018.

       f.   Related Military Skill

            (1) Reconnaissance Marine, 0321.

            (2) COMINT/EW Operator, 2621.



                                          3-158                      Enclosure (1)
 3122                                                               NAVMC 1200.1L



            (3) SIGINT/EW Technician, 2629.

            (4) SIGINT/EW Analyst, 2631.

            (5) Cryptologic Language Analyst, 2641.

            (6) Intelligence Surveillance Reconnaissance (ISR) Systems Engineer,
2651.

            (7) SIGINT/EW Chief, 2691.

            (8) Parachutist, 8023.

            (9) Combatant Diver Marine, 8024.
common_text: CYCBERSPACE OPERATIONS 1. Introduction. The Signals Intelligence (SIGINT), Electromagnetic Warfare (EW) OccFld includes the employment of SIGINT, EW, support to cyberspace operations (CO) and intelligence, surveillance, and reconnaissance (ISR) systems engineering capabilities. Marines in this field are required to set up and operate collection and communications electronic equipment, manage intelligence data, prepare EW and intelligence reports, extend and mesh intelligence services, conduct preventive maintenance on assigned equipment, execute electromagnetic attack (EA), and assist in the operational control and management of SIGINT/EW/CO personnel, equipment, and facilities. Entry- level jobs include Communications Intelligence/Electromagnetic Warfare Operator, Signals Intelligence/Electromagnetic Warfare Analyst, Intelligence Surveillance Reconnaissance Systems Engineer, and Cryptologic Language Analyst. Marines can LATMOV into the 2600 OccFld at the grade of corporal or sergeant. Sergeants requesting LATMOV into the 2600 OccFld must have no more than 1 year time in grade. Duty assignments include Marine Forces Special Operations Command (MARSOC), Marine Corps Information Command (MCIC), Marine Forces Cyber Command (MARFORCYBER), Marine Cryptologic Support Battalion (MCSB), radio battalions, intelligence battalions, infantry battalions, littoral combat team (LCT), marine littoral regiments (MLR), and the staff sections of the MEF information groups (MIG), Marine divisions (MARDIV), and Marine aviation wings (MAW).

nlx_method: NLx employer-demand profiles; private-only ownership unverified. Six-digit profiles pool specialty weighted task incidences after the existing review exclusion mask and five-job task-support floor; destination SOCs require 200 postings and nonzero tasks. Military profiles use binary accepted task presence and the same NLx reference RCA weights as civilian profiles: reciprocal positive task shares (zero weight for reference-absent tasks) of pooled retained support-five NLx weighted incidences across 1,016 reference specialties (912 eligible comparison candidates), sqrt(q * rca_weight), then L2 normalization and cosine. No military crosswalk codes enter the task ranking. All positive top-20 results retained; zero-similarity destinations are not recommendations. Shared field/rating duties are included; general Naval Standards remain separate by paygrade. Summary compares non-future individual source entries (versions can repeat) with nonempty reference sets; grouped, future and general-standard entries remain in all outputs. Hit@k is the fraction with at least one reference SOC recovered; ties are averaged exactly. References outside NLx remain in denominators. DMDC reference status is from July 2024, not current 2026 status.
